newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia '97 coffee production up to 12.8 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Colombia '97 coffee production up to 12.8 mln bags.

text.p: Colombia's coffee production in the 1997 calendar year will increase to as many as 12.8 million 60-kg sacks compared to the 11.6 million 60-kg sacks harvested in the 1996 calendar year, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Thursday.
Exports in 1997 will be 11.6 million 60-kg sacks in 1997 in line with the agreement of the Association of Coffee producing Countries (ACPC).

National Coffee Growers' Federation chief Jorge Cardenas said it was too early to put an exact figure on production for the 1997 calendar year but predicted a minimum of 12.5 million 60-kg sacks and a maximum of 12.8 million 60-kg sacks.

"Production in 1996 was lower than expected which means that part of our exports next year will have to be made up through a reduction in our inventories," Ocampo said after a meeting with Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Committee.
Colombia's coffee inventories currently stand at 6.2 million 60-kg sacks. Those stocks would be cut by about 500,000 60-kg sacks to meet 1997 export commitments, Ocampo said.

A drop in inventories, he said, would reduce the projected deficit of the Coffee Fund, a fund administered by the National Coffee Growers' Federation that guarantees to buy growers' entire crop. The fund deficit was expected to be about $400 million in 1997, according to the Federation. Ocampo said Thursday that figure for 1997 would probably be less than $150 million.
